records.title: Introduction to Social Welfare Practice
records.header: SOC WF 200 Introduction to Social Welfare Practice (5) SSc
records.text: SOC WF 200 Introduction to Social Welfare Practice (5) SSc Introduction to the field of social work, including the theoretical concepts and institutional framework that guide practice. Overview of social work profession and social welfare system within which it operates. Lectures supplemented by exercises, films, guest lectures, and class discussions. Offered: A.

records.header: SOC WF 215 Intergroup Dialogues (3) DIV
records.text: SOC WF 215 Intergroup Dialogues (3) DIV Explores issues of social identities, differences, and inequalities to build understanding, skills, and values for bringing about greater social justice using dialogic communication.

records.title: Writing for Social Welfare
records.header: SOC WF 250 Writing for Social Welfare (1-2, max. 2)
records.text: SOC WF 250 Writing for Social Welfare (1-2, max. 2) Offers an engaging space for social welfare students to develop, practice, and strengthen college-level writing using exercises, discussion, and lecture. Covers summarizing and responding, critical thinking and argument, APA style and academic honesty, as well as language and the writing process. Review of punctuation and mechanics, grammar, and sentence style. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: Mutual Aid, Community Care, and Social Support
records.header: SOC WF 280 Mutual Aid, Community Care, and Social Support (5) SSc
records.text: SOC WF 280 Mutual Aid, Community Care, and Social Support (5) SSc Examines mutual aid and community-based approaches to care and healing. Topics include mutual aid history, peer support, disability justice, survivor-led movements, and social science frameworks for understanding collective responses to trauma and social stress. Offered: AS.

records.title: Social Welfare Practice I
records.header: SOC WF 310 Social Welfare Practice I (5)
records.text: SOC WF 310 Social Welfare Practice I (5) Provides an introduction to the roles, tasks, and functions of the social welfare practitioner and to theories and methods of intervention; a conceptual framework for social work practice with individuals, families, and small groups; and an opportunity to develop skills in problem assessment, intervention, termination, and evaluation. Course equivalent to: TSOCWF 310. Offered: A.

Prerequisite: SOC WF 310. Offered: W.

records.title: Social Welfare Practice III
records.header: SOC WF 312 Social Welfare Practice III (5)
records.text: SOC WF 312 Social Welfare Practice III (5) Focus on macro systems in a diverse society using the generalist perspective. The implications of system resources and configurations for meeting human needs are considered. The role and function of generalist social workers to understand and advocate for system development and change is emphasized. Course equivalent to: TSOCWF 312. Prerequisite: SOC WF 311. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Introduction to Group Work Practice
records.header: SOC WF 313 Introduction to Group Work Practice (5)
records.text: SOC WF 313 Introduction to Group Work Practice (5) Focuses on developing an understanding of both group dynamics and effective leadership and facilitation skills with groups. Students learn about group work from theoretical and empirical literature, as well as intervention models relevant to social work practice. Prerequisite: SOC WF 312. Offered: W.

records.title: Community Service Learning
records.header: SOC WF 315 Community Service Learning (1-5, max. 6)
records.text: SOC WF 315 Community Service Learning (1-5, max. 6) Opportunity for students to apply social work theory to practice, to advocate for social justice, and to be involved in community service. Students learn by connecting classroom theory and community-based experience through the completion of community-based projects in social work-type agencies. Majors only. Offered: WSp.

records.title: Social Welfare Policy
records.header: SOC WF 320 Social Welfare Policy (5) SSc
records.text: SOC WF 320 Social Welfare Policy (5) SSc Emphasizes policy and program development in social welfare with emphasis on the context, making, and unmaking of social policy. Covers policy formulation as well as current and emerging policies in social welfare. Maximum 10 credits allowed between TSOCWF 300; TSOCWF 320; and SOC WF 320. Prerequisite: SOC WF 200. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Introduction to Social Welfare Research
records.header: SOC WF 390 Introduction to Social Welfare Research (5)
records.text: SOC WF 390 Introduction to Social Welfare Research (5) Introduction to logic of the scientific method as applied to social work and social welfare practice, to the design and conduct of a research study, and to data collection and summarization. Skill development in critical consumption of social welfare research. Course equivalent to: TSOCWF 390. Course overlaps with: T CRIM 390. Prerequisite: either EDPSY 490, QMETH 201, STAT 220, STAT 221/CS&SS 221/SOC 221, STAT 290, STAT 390, or STAT 311. Offered: A.

records.title: Human Behavior and Social Environment I
records.header: SOC WF 402 Human Behavior and Social Environment I (5) SSc
records.text: SOC WF 402 Human Behavior and Social Environment I (5) SSc Focuses on understanding human development across the lifespan. Integrates biological, psychological, structural, environmental, political, global, and socio-cultural perspectives. Explores the relationship between the person and the environment including families, groups, organizations, communities, and institutions. Course equivalent to: TSOCWF 402.

records.header: SOC WF 405 Fieldwork Seminar (3)
records.text: SOC WF 405 Fieldwork Seminar (3) Integrates social work practicum experiences with prior and concurrent coursework in social sciences, social work, and research. Includes discussion of class presentations and simulations or practice situations that combine knowledge and skill utilization. Student logs provide a basis for individual goal identification and achievement. Required of social welfare seniors. Course overlaps with: TSOCWF 405. Offered: A.

records.title: Evidence-Based Practices in Social Welfare
records.header: SOC WF 410 Evidence-Based Practices in Social Welfare (3)
records.text: SOC WF 410 Evidence-Based Practices in Social Welfare (3) Focuses on interface between social work research and practice, with attention to origins and defining features of evidence-based practice (EBP) and approaches to intervention consistent with EBP framework. Integrates content on research and practice priorities, and provides students with knowledge and skills to promote use of theory-driven, empirically-supported interventions.

records.text: SOC WF 415 Beginning Field Instruction (1-12, max. 12) Students are placed in selected social service agencies and accept beginning social service assignments under the supervision of competent agency personnel. Course overlaps with: TSOCWF 415. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

records.text: SOC WF 435 Skills for Social Welfare Practice (1) Builds on first-year generalist practice content. Provides skill building in one or two areas of social work practice relevant to many practice settings. Topic chosen by students and faculty. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: W.

records.title: Social Welfare and Artificial Intelligence: Power, Ethics, and Social Impacts
records.header: SOC WF 440 Social Welfare and Artificial Intelligence: Power, Ethics, and Social Impacts (3)
records.text: SOC WF 440 Social Welfare and Artificial Intelligence: Power, Ethics, and Social Impacts (3) Critically engages with how automation technologies interact with social work values of self-determination, equitable access to health and social services, and freedom from violence. Explores how artificial intelligence (AI) tools interact with existing systems of power, who benefits from AI now, and who could in the future. Offered: W.

records.title: Building Competencies for Intergroup Dialogue Facilitation
records.header: SOC WF 442 Building Competencies for Intergroup Dialogue Facilitation (5) A&H/SSc, DIV
records.text: SOC WF 442 Building Competencies for Intergroup Dialogue Facilitation (5) A&H/SSc, DIV Focuses on both knowledge and skills development for peer facilitators. Topics include philosophy and principles of dialogic education and dialogic communication; intergroup communication; social identity development; principles of working with conflict; group dynamics, observation, and facilitation; team building among co-facilitators; and creating a support system among instructors and facilitators.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Facilitating Intergroup Dialogue
records.header: SOC WF 443 Facilitating Intergroup Dialogue (5) A&H/SSc, DIV
records.text: SOC WF 443 Facilitating Intergroup Dialogue (5) A&H/SSc, DIV Practicum seminar providing instruction, consultation, and supervision of peer group facilitators. Focuses on comparison of facilitation experiences and consultations, trouble-shooting with other facilitators, co-facilitator team building, and planning for dialogues. Exploration of specific, current intergroup issues, such as affirmative action and immigration. Continuation of team-building work begun in SOC WF 442.

records.text: SOC WF 450 Integrative Seminar: Poverty Analysis (5) Critical analysis of poverty both in the United States and from a global perspective. Analytical and descriptive focus on measurement, processes of production and perpetuation, and theoretical perspectives that lead to different social and economic policy responses.

records.header: SOC WF 490 Independent Research in Social Welfare (1-15, max. 15)
records.text: SOC WF 490 Independent Research in Social Welfare (1-15, max. 15) Individual work with faculty member to assist with current research project(s). Students trained and supervised in some or all of the following research tasks: literature review, data analysis, record-keeping, interviewing, report writing, data entry and coding, data collection, and other tasks commonly found in research problems in social welfare.
